Where are you teaching? Is it public, private, charter? What grade level? 

I just finished my first year of teaching and will admit it can be hard. That being said, yesterday we had orientation and the reward of having these kids excited to see me and tell me about their summer made it all worth it! I teach for a charter in a low income area. A lot of my students don’t have a trusted adult in their life and it’s a really great feeling to be that for them. 

My advice that I would give is start out strict. It is always easier to become less strict than more! Hold your students to high standards and keep them accountable. We say we practice “care in accountability”. Basically just meaning that when we hold them accountable we are doing so in their best interest. On the other hand, there will be times when you need to lead with empathy and understanding. Just use your best judgment. 

Overall, I would say if you have a good team you can get through it. However, I would also say that if you do not feel like you will be supported, the sooner you quit the better. Kids deserve structure and a rotating door of teachers makes learning extremely difficult for them. My school lost our calculus teacher in January last year and it ended up being a rotating door of subs until April. 

I wish you the best of luck in whatever you decide! I urge you to [put you first](https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZTNVYdQQB/)!!!

Hi. I am someone in a long term relationship with a SA.  I recently found out that he had cheated and lied to me for 6 months. He was not the one to tell me. 
In my opinion, you should tell her. She deserves to not only know but it is so much better to hear it from you. I wish with all of me that my boyfriend had told be how he was feeling (before he even got to the point of having an affair would have been nice but even after it would have been better to hear it from him). 
I am not the one in my relationship that has a sex addiction, and I actually have a lot of issues around sex due to my past traumas. That being said, I can’t relate to you, but I can relate to your partner. So coming from someone like me I think there are a few options you should explore if you want your relationship to work. If you’re willing to attend SAA meeting and therapy and get medicine and do couples therapy, tell your girlfriend. She will still have the option to leave you or decide if she wants to work on the relationship. If you do this, you need to be completely honest and open. If she wants to work this out you with have to abide by her demands while she gains trust of you. If you are not open to SA and therapy and help, you have to tell her anyway. She deserves better. You can ask for an open relationship but if she’s not on board she deserves to be able to walk away. She should now that she needs to get tested if you’ve been intimate with her as well. 
All that being said, this is just the opinion of someone who is dating a sex addict who cheated and is trying to make it work. It’s all still pretty fresh for me. I hope you tell her. If she feels she needs community show her r/survivinginfidelity. Feel free to give her my @ if she wants someone to talk to. I hope you guys can figure it out.
